newsitem.title: Tajikistan: Armed clash near Tajik aluminium producing town. [CORRECTED 13:13 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Armed clash near Tajik aluminium producing town. [CORRECTED 13:13 GMT]

text.p: The commander of the Tajik government's most powerful armoured brigade said his forces clashed with an independent armed band near the aluminium producing town of Tursunzade on Wednesday.
The unauthorised intervention by Colonel Makhmud Khudoyberdyev, who led an anti-government revolt a year ago, prompted apparent alarm among the beleaguered Tajik leadership in the capital Dushanbe.
President Imomali Rakhmonov (corrects surname) ordered the brigade back to barracks.

Torn apart by a four-year civil war, Tajikistan's secular government and its armed Islamist opponents have been holding peace talks in the Iranian capital Tehran this week and a ceasefire between the two sides had appeared to be holding.
"We fought early this morning," Khudoyberdyev told reporters in Shakhrinau, about 12 km (7.5 miles) east of Tursunzade and 45 km (30 miles) west of Dushanbe.
About 10 armoured vehicles and 200 of his men were stationed in Shakhrinau.
Khudoyberdyev said he had moved his troops towards Tursunzade to disarm the band, led by Kodir Abdulayev, because the group had stolen weapons from his men last month.
"They must hand over their weapons. If they do so, we will allow them to leave," said Khudoyberdyev. "If they refuse, we will take tough measures."
One of Abdulayev's men was killed, he added.

Khudoyberdyev apparently acted on his own intiative as Rakhmonov, who is also chief of the Tajik armed forces, ordered the commander back to his base in Kurgan-Tyube, located in the south of the former Soviet republic.
The commander was given until 4 p.m. (1100 GMT) to start pulling out of Shakhrinau.
"If he does not obey orders, his actions will be considered a war crime," Zafar Saidov, Rakhmonov's spokesman, told reporters on Wednesday.
Tursunzade, site of an aluminium smelter which produced 237,000 tonnes of the metal in 1995, has been the scene of clashes between rival armed gangs over the last 12 months.
Khudoyberdyev said his brigade had not targeted the plant but there was no word on whether production had been affected.
